proposal.utterance: Classify 'an act of promising' in BFO terms.

entities.label: ActOfPromising
entities.rationale: An act of promising is a temporally extended happening — a speech act or performative event — that unfolds in time and has a beginning and end. It is not a continuant. It involves an agent (the promisor) and typically an addressee (the promisee) as participants. BFO_0000015 (Process) is the correct type. It is a kind/class because 'an act of promising' names a category of events, not a specific dated occurrence.

entities.label: PromissoryObligation
entities.rationale: An act of promising typically creates an obligation that inheres in the promisor. This obligation is externally grounded in the social/normative context of the promise and is a role borne by the promisor. It is a subclass of the existing working:LegalObligation (itself a subclass of BFO_0000023 Role). This entity is a companion to ActOfPromising: the process realizes the promissory obligation role.

entities.label: PromissoryContent
entities.rationale: Every act of promising conveys a propositional content — what is promised — which can be re-expressed, recorded, or transferred. This informational content is a generically dependent continuant: it is concretely carried by the act and its utterance but is not tied to a single bearer. It is analogous to StatutoryMeaning already in the ontology.

relations.rationale: ActOfPromising is a subclass of Process (BFO_0000015) because it is a temporally extended event.
PromissoryObligation is a species of LegalObligation (itself typed as BFO_0000023 Role), arising specifically from an act of promising.
The process of promising realizes the promissory obligation role borne by the promisor. BFO_0000055 (realizes) connects a process to the realizable entity it brings into effect.
An act of promising has as part the promissory content it conveys; the GDC is concretized in the process.

open_questions: Should ActOfPromising be restricted to legal/institutional promises (creating legally binding obligations) or cover informal moral promises as well? This affects whether PromissoryObligation should be a subclass of LegalObligation or a broader NormativeObligation class.
Is the promisor always a LegalPerson (Material Entity bearing a Role) or should the class allow non-human agents (e.g., corporate entities)? This affects participant typing.
Should PromissoryContent be linked to an existing working:LegalForm or working:Statute class, or kept independent as a standalone GDC class?
proposal.rationale_summary: An act of promising is paradigmatically a BFO Process (BFO_0000015): it is an occurrent that unfolds in time, has a beginning and end, and involves participants (promisor, promisee). Three companion entities are proposed: (1) ActOfPromising as the process class itself; (2) PromissoryObligation as a Role (BFO_0000023) — a realizable entity that is externally grounded in social norms and is borne by the promisor, subclassed under the existing working:LegalObligation; and (3) PromissoryContent as a Generically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000031) representing the propositional content of the promise, which can be abstracted from any particular utterance. The process realizes the obligation (BFO_0000055) and has the content as a part. All three are classes because the utterance uses the indefinite 'an act of promising,' denoting a kind rather than a specific dated event.
